chapter: New Orleans and the tent shows
title: Lee's Creole Belles, the tent shows and first meeting Louis Armstrong
summary: They worked three or four summers as producer for Ed Lee's company under Lou Rose, including tent shows. Billy first met Armstrong when he sang in a boys' vocal quartet before taking up the horn.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, at first, though, this man, Lou Rosen, we were talking about him, who was a, manager of the Dolphin Theater. He had a company there in Orleans called Lee's Creole Bells, run by Ed Lee. Well, Ed Lee had heard so much about us, he wanted to get us to work with him. So we did. And, uh, after he saw that I could produce shows, I was his producer. And I stayed with him. How long did we stay with Ed Lee up there for Lou Rose? Oh, years. Yes, three or four years. Every summer. You know, we just get tired of being black, like here's a monogram.

We just got tired. You know? They just keep you. Yeah. And the people would go to the show and say, is Mac and Mac here? No. Mac's Mary, no. Well, we're not coming. Then we have to come back. Just keep, just coming back, coming back, coming back. Yeah.
Yeah, we worked there at one lot, there at Louisiana Avenue and Howard, for 14 weeks. And then there was another man named Strohler. He was from Algiers, Mr. Strohler.
And he built an air drone over on, on, Jackson.
Jackson and Robinson. Yes, yes, uh-huh.
Did you have sort of a tent too, sometime that you traveled with?

Oh, this was a tent for Lou Rose. Yes, it was. Yes. And we worked around in this air drone for quite a while. And Louis then, and this little Mac, and little Georgia Gray, and, and Happy, they had a little quartet. Now, at this time, none of them were playing drums or horns.

Yes. They'd come up there and sing, haven't you, night sound, why, you know, when I'd have them. And that's where I first met Louis. You went to work? Well, later on when he started playing the horn, then I used him too, you know. But he didn't take up this horn until after he went to this home. He did. And they'd give him these instruments, you know, in order to, you know.
